The statusline is here: https://github.com/RayZ0rr/myNeovim/blob/main/nvim/lua/config/plugins/general/statusline/miniline.lua

Each section can be a table with following fields:
```lua
-- @param string: function or array of functions - If function, should return the section string. Array of function can be used to give smaller versions of the string, in which the first one that fits the window width is selected. Eg :- {filename_func, filenameShort_func}
-- @param hl: optional string - The highlight group
-- @param hl_fn: optional function - A function which returns a highlight group, useful dynamic highlight groups like those based on vim mode
```

Nice! Thanks for sharing!

I didn't look too closely (as it is quite involved), but one thing I noticed is [redundant computations](https://github.com/RayZ0rr/myNeovim/blob/9580c9051ef64769c9099ed807ce0bf4e510dd89/nvim/lua/config/plugins/general/statusline/miniline.lua#L11-L21) (several string concatenations) for cases that are known in advance. This approach makes sense for situations when output values can not be known in advance, but that is not here.

For example, computing a single table values of `vim.fn.mode()` as keys and `color_suffix .. "BoldFg" .. my_utils.vim_mode.colors` as values would make it a single table lookup. As it stands now, these concatenations are done at least on every key press, which is a bit wasteful.

reply_data.body:
> @echasnovski I want to create flexible diagnostics components, like depending on space only show errors, errors + warnings, errors + warnings + info, etc I also want to show the name of the lsp client attached.

Both of these indeed require custom code and are not possible to achieve out of the box with 'minis.statusline'.

> Do you think I can do both without exposing [this private lua table](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L123C1-L123C13) ?

Yes, both of this are possible without exposing private `H` table. All it does for `section_lsp` and `section_diagnostics` is [efficiently track relevant data](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L626-L657) (the tracking part is set up [via autocommands](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L522-L535)) so that they don't have to compute that data on every statusline redraw. The performance gain is not huge, but it was somewhat significant at the time those were implemented (off the top of my head, it was something like couple of microseconds while the whole default active content takes around 25-30 microseconds).

So:
- Instead of [looking at `H.diagnostic_counts` table](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L335) use [`vim.diagnostic.count(buf_id)`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L638).
- Instead of [looking at `H.attached_lsp` table](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L363) use [`vim.lsp.get_clients()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.statusline/blob/e331175f10d9f400b42523b3890841aba202ce16/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L629). Beware that there can be multiple LSP servers attached to the same buffer, which was the main reason of why `section_lsp` only uses `+` signs to display each attached server (otherwise it might and often would become too wide).
reply_data.bodyHTML:
@echasnovski I want to create flexible diagnostics components, like depending on space only show errors, errors + warnings, errors + warnings + info, etc I also want to show the name of the lsp client attached.

Both of these indeed require custom code and are not possible to achieve out of the box with 'minis.statusline'.

Do you think I can do both without exposing this private lua table ?

Yes, both of this are possible without exposing private H table. All it does for section_lsp and section_diagnostics is efficiently track relevant data (the tracking part is set up via autocommands) so that they don't have to compute that data on every statusline redraw. The performance gain is not huge, but it was somewhat significant at the time those were implemented (off the top of my head, it was something like couple of microseconds while the whole default active content takes around 25-30 microseconds).

So:

  • Instead of looking at H.diagnostic_counts table use vim.diagnostic.count(buf_id).
  • Instead of looking at H.attached_lsp table use vim.lsp.get_clients(). Beware that there can be multiple LSP servers attached to the same buffer, which was the main reason of why section_lsp only uses + signs to display each attached server (otherwise it might and often would become too wide).

Beware that there can be multiple LSP servers attached to the same buffer, which was the main reason of why `section_lsp` only uses `+` signs to display each attached server (otherwise it might and often would become too wide).


Yeah, I saw these functions from mini.statusline but I wanted to squeeze out the extra perf from caching
PS: I would also write the function to show '+' if there's more than 1 lsp else show the name of the server
